objectClass.notes: The CC0 side reference strongly establishes profile anatomy, mane layering, scale direction and pedestal. The opposite side is inferred by bilateral symmetry; the exact rear tail transition is only partially visible.

reasoning: The current mascot-like spheres fail because the reference silhouette is a tall tapered fish column supporting an angular lion head, not a round animal body.
The head requires separate brow, muzzle, nose, upper jaw, lower jaw and cavity volumes; the mane is a nested plate system rather than radial spikes.
Overlapping scales, a pectoral fin, tail/wave transition and layered ceramic pedestal are repeated identity systems visible at catalogue distance.

specDepthDecision.rationale: A complex tier is required because the identity rests on continuous organic volumes, deep mouth negative space, layered mane plates and dense repeated scale relief that must hold across multiple angles.

unknownsToResolveBeforeImplementation: The night side-view obscures fine eye carving and exact mouth-cavity depth.
The far side and rear tail transition are inferred by symmetry and supporting searched images.
The model is an intentionally stylised low-poly browser reconstruction, not a scan of Lim Nang Seng's original sculpture.

details.description: Broad swept mane plates form a flattened crown crest behind the brow rather than radial spikes.
A projecting brow plane shades the small inset eye and angles down toward the muzzle.
The muzzle projects forward with a broad rounded nose and downturned upper-lip contour.
A deep open mouth separates upper and lower jaws and contains the water outlet in shadow.
A separate lower jaw and rounded chin project below the water stream and overlap the throat.
Long flattened mane locks sweep from cheek and jaw toward the shoulder in overlapping vertical layers.
details.affects: rear head silhouette and neck overlap

details.description: One tapered pectoral fin projects upward from the front shoulder of the fish body.
Dense overlapping scalloped scales descend in staggered rows around the tapered fish body.
The fish torso narrows steadily toward the pedestal with a slight forward belly curve.
Carved tail and foam ridges blend the lower fish body into the wave pedestal rather than ending as a vertical cylinder.
Several horizontal blue-white wave crests wrap the pedestal in offset layers above the dark plinth.
The white aggregate surface is satin-matte while the blue pedestal mosaic carries tighter low-roughness highlights.
details.scale: macro material split with micro variation

anatomy.note: Only meaningful when objectClass.primaryDomain is character or hybrid. Set applies=true and fill from forge/stage1_intake/extract_landmarks.py. See grimoire/character/reconstruction.md and grimoire/character/likeness_maximization.md.

definitionOfDone: At catalogue-card distance the model reads immediately as Singapore's Merlion: a lion head with open water-spouting jaw and layered mane attached to a tapered overlapping-scale fish body on a blue wave pedestal.
Front, side, rear three-quarter and top-oblique views retain real volume, connected anatomy and a legible mouth cavity; the head must not read as a bear, cat mascot, or sphere with spikes.

featureGroups.name: Lion-head to fish-body silhouette and proportions
qualityCriteria: The head is angular and forward-projecting, the neck/mane overhangs a narrower tapered fish column, and the body terminates in a wave/tail transition instead of a second animal torso.
failureModes: the model reads as a bear or cat mascot
head and body are equal spherical masses
the fish body has no taper or tail transition

featureGroups.name: Brow, muzzle, nose, open jaw and mouth cavity
qualityCriteria: Brow and cheek planes frame small inset eyes; a broad muzzle leads to a projecting upper jaw, separate lower jaw and deep dark mouth cavity aligned with the water emitter.
failureModes: the mouth is a painted dot or closed muzzle
nose and eyes are oversized black mascot features
the water jet exits below or through the chin

featureGroups.name: Layered crown, cheek and rear mane plates
qualityCriteria: Broad swept mane locks overlap from crown to shoulder with directional flow and attached roots; they are flattened sculptural plates, not evenly spaced cones or spikes.
failureModes: mane reads as a ring of spikes
plates float away from the head or intersect the muzzle
rear mane collapses into a smooth helmet

featureGroups.name: Overlapping fish scales, pectoral fin and tail transition
qualityCriteria: Scales overlap in staggered downward-facing rows around the body, a pectoral fin projects from the shoulder, and the lower body blends into a carved tail/wave base with no floating ring ornaments.
failureModes: the body is smooth or furry
the tail and wave base are absent

featureGroups.name: Layered ceramic wave pedestal and water stream
qualityCriteria: The pedestal has multiple horizontal blue mosaic wave crests and a dark plinth; a coherent tapered water curve leaves the mouth cavity and lands beyond the base without reading as a rigid blue pole.
failureModes: pedestal is a plain cyan cylinder
water is an opaque constant-radius rod
wave crests float or fail to wrap the base

visualDeltaChecks: head projection, jaw opening and head-to-body ratio delta
brow, muzzle, nose, eye and mouth-cavity placement delta
mane plate count, direction, overlap and root attachment delta
scale row overlap, fin placement and lower-body taper delta
wave pedestal layering and water-jet origin/arc delta
antiShallowSpecRules: Do not proceed to code if qualityContract.qualityBar is unassessed.
Do not proceed to code if the spec only contains a root component for a moderate or complex object.
Do not proceed to code if required featureGroups are not represented by componentTree, materials, or repetitionSystems.
Do not proceed to code if visible local features are described only in prose and not attached to components/materials/evidenceRefs.
Do not proceed past structural-pass if attached child parts lack attachment.parentSocket, localStart, localEnd, embedDepth/overlap, and gapTolerance.
Do not pass material look-dev when albedo is reused as roughness, height, normal, or AO.
Do not pass material look-dev without macro, meso, and micro surface frequency bands for close-up materials.
Do not pass reference-fidelity material look-dev from a source image without usable referencePbr maps or an explicit documented limitation.
Do not patch a spec with extracted PBR maps when extraction confidence is below the target threshold unless the user explicitly accepts lower fidelity.
Do not place adjacent separate-geometry parts below 0.02 world-unit seam overlap (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).
Do not satisfy raised or recessed relief, fasteners, or grip structure with a map alone when the feature affects form; use geometry or displacement (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).
